aboutMore: (for the record: i do not ONLY listen to one band. i do. but there are other things.) i mow mrs petrovich's lawn on saturdays for $15 and she pays me in lemonade, cookies and the sentence 'you are a deep boy, lucas.' i have never been able to tell if she's joking. my little brother owen (11) and i play mario kart after dinner and it's the one hour a week the pain takes a break (blue shell). my english teacher ms alvarez wrote 'good' next to a line on page 47 and it was NOT the line i thought. i'm still processing. also my mom plays motown while she cooks and i know every harmony. do not repeat that.

blog.title: the lawn is not a metaphor (it's also a lawn)
blog.body: mrs petrovich is 80 and lives 2 houses down and i mow her lawn on saturdays for $15. it's 40 feet by 30. i have measured it. she pays me in lemonade (the powder kind, but with real lemon slices, like it's an event), a plate of kolaczki and the sentence 'you are a deep boy, lucas.' i've been mowing for 11 weeks and i STILL can't tell if she's joking. she calls the notebook 'the diary.' she asked if she's in it. i said no. she said 'good. i'd want editing rights.' i think about that a lot. the lawn is not a metaphor. it keeps growing no matter how i feel and i find that comforting and also offensive. page 52: 'the grass does not know it has been cut.' mrs petrovich read that over my shoulder and said 'it knows. that's why it grows back angry.' that's the best line i've been around all year and it wasn't even mine.

blog.title: page 47: the line she circled
blog.body: ms alvarez gave back 'Trash Night' (i turned it in for extra credit, don't ask) and next to one line there's a green pen circle and the word 'good.' i assumed it was 'the bag is full / so am i.' it was NOT. it was '(i was late)(they started without me).' the parentheses. the part i added at the last second because it was true. she wrote underneath: 'THIS is the real poem. the rest is the costume.' the page has been on my desk for 3 days. i don't know if i'm a poet or just a guy who got to dinner late. i read 'the costume' out loud to the mirror. it's the best criticism i've ever gotten and i want it removed from my record. i also want it framed. both. page 57: 'maybe the truest line is the one you almost cut.' (ms alvarez says show, don't tell. i'm trying. this is me, showing.)

blog.title: blue shell
blog.body: every night after dinner my brother owen (11) and i play mario kart on the gamecube. it's the one hour a week (ok it's 4) the pain takes a break, because it's hard to be tragic when a turtle shell is chasing you. owen always picks rainbow road. i always pick the character who looks the most tired. last night i let him win on the final lap and he put the controller down and said 'you didn't try.' i said 'i'm saving my energy for the pain.' he said 'i'm 11, not dumb.' then he scooted over and said 'you can still sit here even if you're not in the game.' malten i need you to understand that this is the most profound thing anyone has ever said to me and he said it holding a bag of pretzels. page 54: 'the controller is not the point. the couch is.'

blog.title: what my mom plays while she cooks (a confession)
blog.body: my mom cooks on thursdays and plays motown on the little radio in the kitchen. the temptations, marvin gaye, the supremes. i know every harmony. i did not choose to. it's in the walls. last night the radio played 'My Girl' and i was at the table and my mouth just started doing the bass part. i didn't plan it. my mom stopped stirring and turned around and looked at me for about 4 seconds. neither of us said anything. then she turned back around and turned the radio UP. dinner was spaghetti. it was the best dinner of my entire life and i can't explain it. i'm putting this here and NOT in the notebook, because the notebook is for pain and i don't think this was pain. i don't know what this was. i think it might have been fine.
